name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_MATCH_Q01 - SI units of fundamental electrostatic quantities

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities or systems in List-I with their corresponding descriptions, values, or expressions in List-II:

List-I List-II
(A) Electric charge (I) \(\text{N}\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\) or \(\text{V}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}\)
(B) Electric field (II) \(\text{C}\)
(C) Electric flux (III) \(\text{C}\cdot\text{m}\)
(D) Electric dipole moment (IV) \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\) or \(\text{V}\cdot\text{m}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To establish the correct matching between List-I and List-II, we evaluate the scientific definition, formula, or law governing each item in List-I individually.

Step 2: Analysis of Electric charge
For Electric charge, it is measured in coulombs (\(\text{C}\)) in the SI system.

Step 3: Analysis of Electric field
For Electric field, it is defined as force per unit charge (\(\text{N}\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\)) or electric potential gradient (\(\text{V}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}\)).

Step 4: Analysis of Electric flux
For Electric flux, it is defined by the surface integral of the electric field, giving units of \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\) or \(\text{V}\cdot\text{m}\).

Step 5: Analysis of Electric dipole moment
For Electric dipole moment, it is the product of charge and separation vector, giving units of \(\text{C}\cdot\text{m}\).

Step 6: Matching Conclusion
Combining all the individual pairings yields the set of relations: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_MATCH_Q02 - Dimensional formulas of electrostatic physical quantities

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities or systems in List-I with their corresponding descriptions, values, or expressions in List-II:

List-I List-II
(A) Electric charge (I) \([\text{M}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}]\)
(B) Electric field (II) \([\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^{-3}\text{T}^4\text{A}^2]\)
(C) Electric flux (III) \([\text{T}\text{A}]\)
(D) Permittivity of free space (\(\varepsilon_0\)) (IV) \([\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}]\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To establish the correct matching between List-I and List-II, we evaluate the scientific definition, formula, or law governing each item in List-I individually.

Step 2: Analysis of Electric charge
For Electric charge, it is given by current times time, \(q = I t\), yielding the dimensional formula \([\text{T}\text{A}]\).

Step 3: Analysis of Electric field
For Electric field, it is given by \(F/q = [\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}]/[\text{T}\text{A}] = [\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}]\).

Step 4: Analysis of Electric flux
For Electric flux, it is given by \(E \times \text{Area} = [\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}][\text{L}^2] = [\text{M}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}]\).

Step 5: Analysis of Permittivity of free space (\(\varepsilon_0\))
For Permittivity of free space (\(\varepsilon_0\)), it is from Coulomb's law \(\varepsilon_0 = \frac{q^2}{4\pi F r^2} = \frac{[\text{T}\text{A}]^2}{[\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}][\text{L}^2]} = [\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^{-3}\text{T}^4\text{A}^2]\).

Step 6: Matching Conclusion
Combining all the individual pairings yields the set of relations: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Final Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_MATCH_Q03 - Distance dependence of electrostatic field configurations

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities or systems in List-I with their corresponding descriptions, values, or expressions in List-II:

List-I List-II
(A) Point electric charge (I) Independent of distance \(r\)
(B) Short electric dipole (II) \(E \propto \frac{1}{r}\)
(C) Infinitely long straight charged wire (III) \(E \propto \frac{1}{r^3}\)
(D) Infinite uniformly charged thin plane sheet (IV) \(E \propto \frac{1}{r^2}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To establish the correct matching between List-I and List-II, we evaluate the scientific definition, formula, or law governing each item in List-I individually.

Step 2: Analysis of Point electric charge
For Point electric charge, it is the electric field follows the inverse square law \(E = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{r^2}\), so \(E \propto \frac{1}{r^2}\).

Step 3: Analysis of Short electric dipole
For Short electric dipole, it is at distances much greater than the dipole size (\(r \gg 2a\)), the fields of the two charges largely cancel, resulting in \(E \propto \frac{1}{r^3}\).

Step 4: Analysis of Infinitely long straight charged wire
For Infinitely long straight charged wire, it is Gauss's law gives \(E = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 r}\), which shows that \(E \propto \frac{1}{r}\).

Step 5: Analysis of Infinite uniformly charged thin plane sheet
For Infinite uniformly charged thin plane sheet, it is Gauss's law gives \(E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\), which is uniform and independent of distance \(r\).

Step 6: Matching Conclusion
Combining all the individual pairings yields the set of relations: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

Final Answer: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_MATCH_Q04 - Electrostatic systems and corresponding governing expressions

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities or systems in List-I with their corresponding descriptions, values, or expressions in List-II:

List-I List-II
(A) Torque on dipole in uniform electric field (I) \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{r^2}\)
(B) Field on axis of short dipole at distance \(r\) (II) \(\mathbf{p} \times \mathbf{E}\)
(C) Field inside thin spherical shell of radius \(R\) (\(r < R\)) (III) Zero
(D) Field outside thin spherical shell of total charge \(q\) (\(r \ge R\)) (IV) \(\frac{2\mathbf{p}}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To establish the correct matching between List-I and List-II, we evaluate the scientific definition, formula, or law governing each item in List-I individually.

Step 2: Analysis of Torque on dipole in uniform electric field
For Torque on dipole in uniform electric field, it is the couple formed by equal and opposite forces produces torque \(\boldsymbol{\tau} = \mathbf{p} \times \mathbf{E}\).

Step 3: Analysis of Field on axis of short dipole at distance \(r\)
For Field on axis of short dipole at distance \(r\), it is given by \(\mathbf{E} = \frac{2\mathbf{p}}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}\) pointing along the direction of the dipole moment vector.

Step 4: Analysis of Field inside thin spherical shell of radius \(R\) (\(r < R\))
For Field inside thin spherical shell of radius \(R\) (\(r < R\)), it is the Gaussian surface inside the shell encloses zero net charge, hence \(E = 0\).

Step 5: Analysis of Field outside thin spherical shell of total charge \(q\) (\(r \ge R\))
For Field outside thin spherical shell of total charge \(q\) (\(r \ge R\)), it is by Gauss's law the external field behaves as if the entire charge were at the center: \(E = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{r^2}\).

Step 6: Matching Conclusion
Combining all the individual pairings yields the set of relations: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.

Final Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
